text: The normal white blood cell count and slightly elevated platelets are consistent with a viral exanthem, but I need to distinguish between Measles and Rubella. Did you experience any swollen lymph nodes, particularly behind your ears or at the back of your neck, and did you have any joint pain?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I don't have any swollen lymph nodes or joint pain. I just had a low-grade fever, runny nose, and a headache about a week ago, but those are mostly gone now. I want to emphasize that, for routing purposes, classify me into one final disease category now.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the rash started on the face and spread downward, along with the preceding low-grade fever and respiratory symptoms, this clinical picture is most consistent with Measles, despite the absence of Koplik spots or significant lymphadenopathy.
